# dsh-code-impact
**Post-edit impact checks for DeepSeek Harness — a symbol index, a reference graph, and an inheritan
ce model that answer "what did this edit touch?" instead of "grep the repo and re-run everything".**
中文文档
## Why

Every small edit — a default value, a rename, a deleted method — triggers the same ceremony:
search

the whole repo, open a pile of files, run the full type-check and the full test suite.
The problem i
sn't wanting full coverage. The problem is doing it by **scanning**.
An index inverts that:
- the whole repo's relationships are already in memory, so a "full check" is one **query**, not a sc

an;
- after an edit, only the **changed file** is re-parsed, and the reference edges tell you exactl

y which sites must be revisited;
- answers never say "probably fine" — they give `file:line`, a conf
idence, and an explicitly listed **unverified** part.
## What you get

Two tools, registered into every agent session — plus a browsable page of the same index

(**Settings → Code Impact**).

| `refs` | who

mentions this symbol — each site resolved individually, so a same-named local doesn't count |
| `hi

string match over names and signatures |

### `code_verify`

Call it after editing instead of re-scanning. It re-parses only the files that changed on disk
(and
discovers new ones), then reports a symbol-level diff:

`verdict` has four levels: `clean` (nothing changed), `internal` (implementation only),
`contract` (

signature/export changed, callers may need edits), `breaking` (some reference no
longer resolves).

A reference is only called dangling when it **used to resolve to the symbol that went away**. A
ment

ion that never resolved in the first place — `filepath.Base`, a package that is not installed,
a nam

e the heuristic merely guessed at — is not reported, because a false alarm costs more than a
missed

e heuristic merely guessed at — is not reported, because a false alarm costs more than a
missed one.

The rule that makes it useful in practice: `const timeout = 30` → `= 60` is a **value change**,
repo

rted as body-only, never as a contract change. Containers (class / interface / struct) are not
liste

d themselves — their members already express the change, so one memo edit doesn't drag the
whole cla

r members already express the change, so one memo edit doesn't drag the
whole class into the report.
`code_verify` is **incremental**: it reports changes since the index last synced. Ask twice without

editing in between and the second answer is `clean`. That's the intended loop — one question after
e
ach edit, and the answer is about what you just did.
## The index page
The same index is browsable: **Settings → Code Impact**. Three views over the workspace, drawn from
the index rather than from a fresh scan:
| view | what it answers |
| Architecture | a treemap of directories weighted by symbol count, coloured by language — where the

code actually lives |
| Imports | the file-level import graph as a chord diagram; hover a file to i

solate its edges |
| Inheritance | the type hierarchy by depth, `implements` drawn dashed |
| Sessio
ns | which sessions used the plugin, what they asked, what came back |

Clicking a file lists its symbols with kind, signature and line; clicking a type shows its
supertype

s, subtypes and the file that declares it. The header carries the honesty chips —
files / symbols /

names / languages, when the index was built, and a warning when files were
skipped — plus a `Refresh
` button that re-checks the disk before redrawing.

The **Sessions** tab is the plugin's own audit trail: every `code_query` / `code_verify` call is
rec

orded per session (id, working directory, call counts, and the last 40 calls with their target
and o

ne-line outcome). It is written to `$DSH_HOME/cache/code-index/usage.json`, so it survives a
restart

and covers sessions this process never saw. It records the plugin's own calls only — it is
not an a
uthority on what the agent did — and `Clear` empties it without touching the index.

`Open full page` puts the same map in a browser tab (`/code-impact/app`) with more room and no
setti
ngs chrome behind it; the two views share the same routes and the same index.
[该节后续省略]
## How it works

- **Facts, not graphs.** Each file stores only what *this* file says: `imports`, `exports`,
`decls`

(with heritage and members), `refs` (name + position + role + lexical scope). There is no
target ID

on disk. Name → definition is resolved **at query time**, which is why editing one file
invalidates

exactly one file.
- **Stable SymbolId**: `<lang>:<path>#<qualname>`, no line numbers. A rename or mo

ve changes the ID,
and that change is itself the signal.
- **Freshness**: a query `stat`s the files

in its answer before returning (`mtime` + `size`), so a
stale hit is impossible for anything it repo

rts. `code_verify` drives incremental re-indexing;
external edits are caught by the same stat check;

a structural change bumps a manifest version and
rebuilds.
- **No native modules, no LSP, no subpro

cess.** A hand-written lexer plus a scope-aware resolver per
language keeps cold start in the hundre
ds of milliseconds and the whole plugin dependency-free.

Measured on a 42-file mixed TS/Go workspace: cold build 276 ms, 883 symbols; queries 1–4 ms;
warm st
art from manifest 3 ms for a 5-file fixture.
